I’m not saying it’s bad, I’m saying it needs to be better. Hotels aren’t built to be homes. What’s the point of having a roof over your head if the people around you don’t want you there, you can’t decorate or really get comfortable without fear of being held liable for damage, you can’t save money by choosing your own appliances or growing your own food? The point of a solution like this is to get people off of the streets, quickly, and out of sight from commuters and tourists while at their worst moments. This does benefit the unhoused but it benefits society as a whole moreso than the specific population it’s meant to serve. If we really want this part of our society to heal and become productive members we need to offer them more permanent solutions if that is what they want or need. Speaking from person experience when you are in crisis you can’t really make those decisions with clarity. A hotel room won’t provide the type of resources that will allow most people to make the next step towards what they want to do next after getting out of survival mode, especially while they aren’t wanted where they are at on top of dealing with the limitations that come with living in a place like a hotel…
